title: Python Lessons
description: Python materials for Accepted EBS members, shared by the organizing team. Sign in with an accepted account to see the latest lessons and updates.

title: EBS Organizers and Faculty Advisors
description: Meet the student organizers and faculty advisors behind EBS, led by the Genetics and Biotechnology Club at Phillips Exeter Academy in New Hampshire.

title: Exeter Biology Symposium 2027
description: Free dry-lab biology research for middle and high school students. Present a poster at EBS on April 25, 2027, in Exeter, New Hampshire, or online.

title: About EBS and Dry-Lab Research
description: Discover EBS, a free biology symposium and dry-lab research program organized by students at Phillips Exeter Academy with faculty guidance.

title: Provisional Symposium Schedule
description: View the provisional April 25, 2027 EBS schedule in Eastern Time: keynote, poster sessions, judging, and closing ceremony at Phillips Exeter Academy and online.

title: Apply to EBS
description: Choose a student, school, or judge application for EBS 2027. Sign in and submit the Google Form; creating an account does not submit an application.

title: Dataset Library
description: Guides to esquisse, Galaxy, iDEP and biblioshiny, and free datasets for research in 14 fields, from systems biology and microbiome science to bibliometrics and meta-analysis.

title: Member Open Source Resources
description: Accepted EBS members can explore community datasets, code, and curriculum materials through EBS Open Source. Sign in to access the linked project tools.

title: Student Projects and Research Deadlines
description: Explore EBS dry-lab projects and checkpoints: idea and plan, research abstract and all code, then a first poster draft, with feedback from all four co-heads.

title: No-Code Research Projects and Cohorts
description: Find a six-week, no-code biology research project. Answer five quick questions to match with a Galaxy, iDEP, or Biblioshiny cohort, then sign up.

title: Research Resources
description: Research materials for Accepted EBS members, shared by the organizing team. Sign in with an accepted account to view the latest resources.

title: Student Applications
description: Apply to present original biology research at EBS 2027, in person or online. Wet-lab projects will be accepted on a case-by-case basis. Participation is free.

title: School Registration
description: Sign your school up for EBS, or provide a contact person if EBS has already contacted you. Find guidance on individual student signup and Zoom orientation.

title: Coding Lessons
description: Coding materials for Accepted EBS members, shared by the organizing team. Sign in with an accepted account to see the latest lessons and updates.

title: EBS Participation and Signup FAQ
description: Find answers about EBS project eligibility, case-by-case wet-lab acceptance, costs, registration, Zoom orientation, and attendance.

title: R and RStudio Lessons
description: R and RStudio materials for Accepted EBS members, shared by the organizing team. Sign in with an accepted account to see the latest lessons and updates.

title: Judge Applications
description: Apply to judge student biology research at EBS on April 25, 2027. Review poster presentations and give constructive feedback in person or online.

title: Account and Approval Status
description: Check your EBS approval status and get application help. Accepted participants can create a research folder and find research, resource, and presentation guidance.

title: Contact the EBS Team
description: Contact the EBS organizing team with questions about participation, student research, applications, account access, or events. Find answers in our FAQ.

title: Member Events
description: Sign in with an accepted Exeter Biology Symposium account to access member events. Contact the organizing team if you need help with account access.

title: Terms of Use and Research Ownership
description: Read EBS terms on participation, adult supervision, research integrity and ownership, accounts, research folders, and use of symposium resources.

title: Privacy Notice and Website Data
description: Learn how EBS handles account and application information, contact messages, research folders, and website data, including hosting and analytics.
